metadata.title: Generation per Production Type and Exchange
metadata.description:
Production per fuel, exchange and total consumption per bidding zone.

The dataset combines fast updated data with more correct settlement data. Only the best data is shown per time period. No filters are needed.
metadata.comment:
Versions:
* Initial: Based on online power signal to Energinet's SCADA system. Published shortly after end of period. Errors will occur, and will generally not be corrected.
* Preliminary: Based on settlement data, however divided on fuels based on last year data per power plant. 8-10 days delay.
* Final: Based on settlement data, division on fuels based on data per power plant in the relevant year. Published June 1 the following year.

---
**API Request Frequency** \
To get the most up-to-date data, calling the API with a dynamic timestamp such as [start=now-P1D](https://api.energidataservice.dk/dataset/GenerationProdTypeExchange?start=now-P1D) is a good approach. Making a few requests hourly is sufficient to ensure getting the latest data.
metadata.caution:
The dataset will change as part of the [transition to DataHub 3.0](https://www.energidataservice.dk/news#154).\
The URL/endpoint will remain unchanged. However, the values will be calculated using a different method. 
We are aware that the values do not exactly match those reported under Article 16.1b&c on the Transparency Platform, and we are currently investigating a solution.

**Expected implementation date: October / November.**
metadata.author: Energinet

columns.description: A date and time shown in _UTC time zone_. It is the "from" timestamp for the period in which the values are valid. The dataset resolution sets the length of the interval.
columns.comment:
Please note that the _format_ shown in the example applies to data downloaded as JSON or fetched through the API.
The format is slightly different when it is shown on screen or downloaded manually as CSV or XLSX. This is mainly due to readability and consideration for Excel users.

**In preview (in the GUI)** all timestamps are shown as (display convention)
YYYY-MM-DD hh:mmZ
e.g. 2017-07-14 08:00Z. 
That is without the seconds. The Z will remind viewers that this is UTC.

In **download (CSV and XLSX)** the date time are exported as
YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm
e.g. 2017-07-14 08:00.
That is without the “T” and the “Z” and the seconds. Excel will recognize it as date-time. The user must remember the convention about time zones.

In **download (JSON and API)** the datetime is exported as
YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss
e.g. 2017-07-14T08:00:00.
That is without the "Z".

columns.description: The version of the declaration.
columns.comment:
"Initial" is based on live production measurement on larger production facilities, and upscaled. Power plant data is based on the latest fuel count. The fuel count may be up to 1,5 years old, but normally relatively stable per power plant per kWh.

"Preliminary" is based on settlement production data (at least 8 days delay), but still with Power plant data the latest fuel count from previous years (up to -2 years).

"Final" is based on settlement production data, and with Power plant data from the fuel count same year. The final version is published June 1 at the latest for the previous year.

columns.description: Electricity production from solar power.

The estimated production from solar panels, which is not  delivered to the grid. The value is the difference between the modelled (expected) production and the actual delivered production from solar panels. When the modelled value is smaller than the actual value, the local power self-consumption is set to zero.
Average power production from power plants with biomass as main fuel.
columns.comment: Note that the statistics are based on the main fuel in master data. The power plants can supplement with other fuels and therefore the data will not be completely compliant with the final fuel count.

metadata.title: Day-Ahead Prices
metadata.description:
Day-Ahead Prices for Denmark and Neighboring Countries.

This dataset provides day-ahead electricity prices for Denmark (DK1 and DK2) and neighboring countries in the Nord Pool market, including Norway, Sweden, Finland, and Germany. In the day-ahead market, participants buy and sell electricity for delivery the following day within their respective bidding zones.
metadata.comment:
The day-ahead prices reflect the balance between supply and demand and serve as a key indicator of market dynamics across the Nordic and European power systems.

The Day-Ahead Price (DKK) is calculated based on the Day-Ahead Price (EUR) and the Euro exchange rate from Danmarks Nationalbank. It may therefore deviate from Danish Day-Ahead prices seen elsewhere.

For data before 2025-10-01 see [Elspot Prices](https://www.energidataservice.dk/tso-electricity/Elspotprices) (hourly resolution).

---
**API Request Frequency** \
To get the Day-Ahead Prices for tomorrow, calling the API with a dynamic timestamp such as [start=StartOfDay%2BP1D](https://api.energidataservice.dk/dataset/DayAheadPrices?start=StartOfDay%2BP1D) is a good approach. Making a request every five minutes or so between 13:00 and 14:00 CET is sufficient to ensure getting the latest data.
